title: Minimum Elements to Add to Form a Given Sum
statement: Every value in the integer array `nums` lies between `-limit` and `limit` (inclusive). You may append integers to `nums`, and each appended integer `x` must obey the same bound, `abs(x) <= limit`. Return the smallest number of integers you have to append so that the sum of the whole array becomes exactly `goal` (this is `0` when the sum already equals `goal`).
signature: int minElements(int[] nums, int limit, int goal)
notes:
## Intuition

The values already in `nums` cannot change, so only their total matters: the appended values must make up the difference `goal - sum`. Its sign does not matter either, since flipping every appended value flips their total, so we need the fewest values in `[-limit, limit]` adding up to `gap = abs(goal - sum)`. Each value contributes at most `limit`, so `k` values reach at most `k * limit`, which means at least `ceil(gap / limit)` are needed. That many are also enough: use `limit` for all but one and let the last one cover the remainder, which is between `0` and `limit`.

(Adding one value at a time, each as large as allowed, gives the same count but can take about 10^9 steps.)

## Approach

1. Add up `nums` into `sum`.
2. Compute `gap = Math.abs(goal - sum)`, the amount the appended values must cover.
3. Return `Math.ceil(gap / limit)`, which is `0` when `gap` is `0`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, -1, 1]`, so `sum = 1`. With `goal = -4`, `gap = abs(-4 - 1) = 5`. With `limit = 3`, `5 / 3 = 1.67`, which rounds up to `2`: append `-3` and `-2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) to add up `nums`.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- `sum` can reach 10^11 in size, beyond a 32-bit integer; Java and C solutions need a 64-bit type for `sum` and `gap`.
- Use a ceiling, not plain integer division: a remainder still needs one more value. In integer arithmetic write `(gap + limit - 1) / limit`.
- Take the absolute value before dividing; a negative `gap` with a ceiling gives the wrong count.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sum` | total of the values already in `nums` |
| `num` | the value being added to `sum` |
| `gap` | how far `sum` is from `goal` |

narration.2: Only the total of the existing values matters.
narration.4: ...and add it to the running total.
narration.6: The appended values must make up this distance, in whichever direction.
narration.7: Each appended value covers at most limit, so round the number of full limits up.
